question.:question/problem: Given that $h(x)=-7{x}^{2}-3x+2{e}^{x}$, find the slope of the tangent at $x=0.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, using the addition and the power rules, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-7{x}^{2}-3x+2{e}^{x}) \\  & =-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(7{x}^{2})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3x)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{e}^{x}) \\  & =-7\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2})-3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x)+2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x}) \\  & =-14x-3+2{e}^{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=0} & ={(-14x-3+2{e}^{x})\,|}_{x=0} \\  & =-14\cdot 0-3+2{e}^{0} \\  & =-3+2\cdot 1 \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Given that $g(x)=-3{e}^{x}+5{x}^{2}$, find the slope of the tangent at $x=0.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, using the addition and the power rules, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-3{e}^{x}+5{x}^{2}) \\  & =-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{e}^{x})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5{x}^{2}) \\  & =-3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x})+5\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}) \\  & =-3{e}^{x}+5(2x) \\  & =-3{e}^{x}+10x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=0} & ={(-3{e}^{x}+10x)\,|}_{x=0} \\  & =-3{e}^{0}+10\cdot 0 \\  & =-3\cdot 1-0 \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$
